        How these numbers are worked out
        Source
        BP-Ontrac Team Metrics for the Broward and Dade team, pulled one fiscal month at a time and one week at a time.
        Fiscal month
        The 22nd of one month to the 21st of the next, named for the month it ends in. The latest month runs to the most recent day BP-Ontrac allows.
        Team totals
        FTR is FTR fails out of all jobs, and tool usage is each tech’s rate weighted by their jobs, the same way as the company website. El FTR son las fallas de FTR sobre todos los trabajos, y el uso de herramientas es la tasa de cada técnico ponderada por sus trabajos, igual que en el sitio web de la compañía. FTR se echèk FTR sou tout travay yo, epi itilizasyon zouti se to chak teknisyen selon kantite travay li, menm jan ak sit entènèt konpayi an. Counts are added across techs before the rate is worked out, so busier techs carry more weight.
        Targets
        Tool usage —, tNPS —, FTR —.
        tNPS 3 mo
        Promoters minus detractors over all surveys in the last three fiscal months, which steadies small monthly samples. A tech’s monthly tNPS counts as a miss only with at least 5 surveys that month.
        Rank
        Same score as Market leaders over the timeframe on the slider: 60% FTR, 30% tNPS and 10% tool usage, with small samples pulled toward the team average. Techs with no jobs in the timeframe aren’t ranked.
        Tool usage fails
        Jobs this fiscal month where tool usage was required but not done.
        tNPS fails
        Detractor surveys (scores of 0 to 6) the tech got this fiscal month.
        FTR fails
        Jobs this fiscal month that did not count as a first-time fix.
        Promoters to target
        How many promoter surveys (scores of 9 or 10) in a row the tech needs, with no detractors, to bring this month’s tNPS up to target. Passives (7 or 8) don’t subtract, but they still count as surveys, so they pull tNPS down.
        Fixes to target
        How many first-time fixes in a row the tech needs, with no repeats, to bring this month’s FTR up to target.
        Repeat rate
        Repeat visits as a share of trouble calls.
        Rework rate
        Rework as a share of installs and trouble calls.
        PHT pass rate
        Premise health tests without a failure, as a share of all tests.
        Weekly view
        A week counts as too small to judge with fewer than 10 FTR jobs, 3 surveys or 8 trouble calls.
        Left out
        Tech 7026 shows jobs but no tool usage, survey or FTR data, so it is not included.
